suggestions.reason: The clause incorporates Exhibit A by reference but does not state what falls outside the scope of Contract Services, leaving both parties without a defined boundary between in-scope obligations and additional-services requests. Compounding this, the evidence indicates that Exhibit A uses the phrase "Consultant's scope of services shall include," which implies a non-exhaustive list and creates ambiguity about whether unlisted activities are automatically within scope or require a supplemental agreement. Practically, this exposes the Consultant to demands for unlisted work without additional compensation, while simultaneously leaving the City uncertain as to what it has contracted for. A single clarifying sentence expressly designating services not set forth in Exhibit A as out-of-scope resolves both issues and reinforces the supplemental agreement mechanism already in the clause.
suggestions.original_text: Scope of Services. Consultant shall perform those services (“Contract Services”) described under Scope of Services in Exhibit A, which is attached to this Agreement and incorporated herein by reference. The City may also request additional services not anticipated at the time of this Agreement. At the City’s request, the Consultant shall submit a written scope of the additional work including an estimate of additional costs for the performance of the additional work. No change in scope shall be effective nor additional compensation be paid, except on the basis of the provisions of a written supplemental agreement or an amendment signed by the Parties.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Scope of Services. Consultant shall perform those services ("Contract Services") described under Scope of Services in Exhibit A, which is attached to this Agreement and incorporated herein by reference. Services not expressly set forth in Exhibit A are outside the scope of Contract Services. The City may also request additional services not anticipated at the time of this Agreement. At the City's request, the Consultant shall submit a written scope of the additional work including an estimate of additional costs for the performance of the additional work. No change in scope shall be effective nor additional compensation be paid, except on the basis of the provisions of a written supplemental agreement or an amendment signed by the Parties.

suggestions.reason: Section 3 as drafted contains no operative payment mechanics whatsoever: it states only that the City shall pay the Consultant "as set forth in Exhibit A," without specifying how or when invoices are issued, when payment falls due, how fees are calculated or whether they are fixed, what happens if an invoice is disputed, or what consequences follow late payment. This level of incompleteness creates material enforceability risk for both parties — the Consultant cannot point to a contractual trigger for payment, and the City has no mechanism to contest an erroneous charge or cap its exposure to fee escalation. The absence of an expense-approval mechanism similarly leaves both parties without clarity on what costs are recoverable and who bears them. Because Exhibit A is the operative financial schedule, it must be aligned to any payment mechanics inserted here to avoid a conflict between the two provisions.
suggestions.original_text: SECTION 3. Compensation and Expenses. As set forth in Exhibit A, the City shall pay the Consultant for the Contract Services it performs as outlined in Section 2 of this Agreement.
suggestions.suggested_fix: SECTION 3. Compensation and Expenses. As set forth in Exhibit A, the City shall pay the Consultant for the Contract Services outlined in Section 2 at the rates specified in Exhibit A, which rates shall remain fixed unless amended in writing by both parties. The Consultant shall submit invoices to the City in accordance with the schedule set forth in Exhibit A, and the City shall pay all undisputed amounts within thirty (30) days of receipt. The City may dispute any invoice in writing within ten (10) days of receipt, identifying the disputed amount and basis therefor; undisputed portions shall remain due and payable as provided herein. Undisputed amounts not paid within thirty (30) days of receipt shall accrue interest at the rate specified in Exhibit A. Pre-approved, documented expenses shall be reimbursed by the City in accordance with Exhibit A.

suggestions.reason: The clause creates several commercially significant gaps. First, the City's termination "for cause" right is undefined and contains no cure period, meaning the City could terminate immediately for a minor or disputed breach without first giving the Consultant an opportunity to remedy it. Second, the Consultant's termination right is limited to convenience only, with no reciprocal right to terminate for the City's material breach, which is an imbalance that is not commercially justified in a bilateral professional services arrangement. Finally, neither party's provision expressly states when termination takes effect, which creates potential disputes about payment obligations and transition periods.
suggestions.original_text: SECTION 4. Termination of Agreement. The City may terminate this Agreement at any time on and after November 30, 2024, with sixty (60) days’ written notice for convenience or cause upon written notice to Consultant. If the City terminates the Agreement under this Section, the City shall pay the Consultant for Contract Services satisfactorily performed by Consultant before the termination, and for all associated expenses incurred by the Consultant before the termination. Under no circumstances will the Consultant be entitled to anticipatory profits or consequential damages. Consultant may terminate the agreement at any time upon sixty (60) days’ written notice. The provisions regarding indemnity and insurance shall survive the termination of this Agreement.
suggestions.suggested_fix: SECTION 4. Termination of Agreement. The City may terminate this Agreement at any time on and after November 30, 2024, for convenience upon sixty (60) days' written notice to Consultant, or for cause if Consultant fails to cure a material breach within thirty (30) days of written notice thereof. If the City terminates the Agreement under this Section, the City shall pay the Consultant for Contract Services satisfactorily performed by Consultant before the termination, and for all associated expenses incurred by the Consultant before the termination. Under no circumstances will the Consultant be entitled to anticipatory profits or consequential damages. Consultant may terminate this Agreement for convenience at any time upon sixty (60) days' written notice, or for cause if the City fails to cure a material breach within thirty (30) days of written notice thereof. Termination shall take effect upon expiration of the applicable notice period. The provisions regarding indemnity and insurance shall survive the termination of this Agreement.

suggestions.reason: The clause as drafted imposes compliance obligations solely on the Consultant, with no corresponding obligation on the City, creating a bilateral imbalance that is commercially unfair in a Professional Services Agreement. It omits any reference to anti-bribery and anti-corruption laws or applicable supply chain labor standards, leaving both parties exposed to regulatory and reputational risk. The clause also contains no requirement for either party to notify the other upon discovering a breach of applicable law that materially affects the Agreement, undermining operational transparency and limiting the other party's ability to mitigate harm. The phrase "applicable at the time the Consultant conducts the Contract Services" creates ambiguity as to whether the Consultant must adapt to changes in law during performance, without addressing cost allocation for such changes.
suggestions.original_text: SECTION 6. Compliance with Laws. Consultant shall comply with local, state, and federal rules, regulations, and laws pertaining to this Agreement that are applicable at the time the Consultant conducts the Contract Services, regardless of whether such requirements are specifically referred to in this Agreement. Consultant shall defend, indemnify, and hold harmless the City, its elected officials, officers, employees, and agents against any claim or liability arising from or based on any violation of the same.
suggestions.suggested_fix: SECTION 6. Compliance with Laws. Each Party shall comply with all applicable local, state, and federal rules, regulations, and laws pertaining to this Agreement, including anti-bribery, anti-corruption, and applicable supply chain labor standards, regardless of whether such requirements are specifically referred to in this Agreement. Each Party shall promptly notify the other in writing of any breach of applicable law that materially affects this Agreement. Consultant shall defend, indemnify, and hold harmless the City, its elected officials, officers, employees, and agents against any claim or liability arising from or based on any violation by Consultant of the same.

suggestions.clause: Compliance with Equal Opportunity Laws, Regulations, and Rules
suggestions.reason: The clause addresses discrimination obligations in reasonable detail but omits three commercially material compliance elements that represent significant legal exposure for both parties: there is no anti-bribery or anti-corruption obligation, no requirement for either party to notify the other upon becoming aware of a material breach of applicable law affecting the Agreement, and no acknowledgment of supply-chain labor standards addressing forced labor or human trafficking. The absence of a notification obligation in particular means that a material compliance failure could continue undetected and unmitigated, increasing liability exposure for both parties. These gaps collectively leave the compliance framework materially incomplete against market-standard professional services contracting practice.
suggestions.original_text: Discrimination Prohibited. Consultant agrees to comply with the Kansas Act Against Discrimination (K.S.A. 44-1001 et seq.) and the Kansas Age Discrimination in Employment Act (K.S.A. 44-1111 et seq.) and shall not discriminate against any person in the performance of work under this Agreement because of race, religion, color, sex, disability, national origin or ancestry, or age.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Discrimination Prohibited. Consultant agrees to comply with the Kansas Act Against Discrimination (K.S.A. 44-1001 et seq.) and the Kansas Age Discrimination in Employment Act (K.S.A. 44-1111 et seq.) and shall not discriminate against any person in the performance of work under this Agreement because of race, religion, color, sex, disability, national origin or ancestry, or age. Consultant shall further comply with all applicable anti-bribery and anti-corruption laws and shall take commercially reasonable steps to prevent forced labor and human trafficking in its supply chain. Each party shall promptly notify the other in writing upon becoming aware of any material breach of applicable law that affects this Agreement.

suggestions.reason: The clause requires Consultant to maintain insurance "throughout the duration of this Agreement" but imposes no post-termination or post-expiration tail period, leaving both parties exposed to latent claims—particularly professional liability or occurrence-based claims—that may arise after the Agreement ends but relate to work performed under it. Additionally, the clause is silent on the relationship between insurance coverage and contractual liability, creating ambiguity as to whether the specified coverage amounts operate as a ceiling on either party's obligations; without a non-limitation statement, one party could argue that insurance proceeds satisfy or cap the other's liability exposure. Both gaps are market-standard items in professional services agreements and present a bilateral enforceability risk.
suggestions.original_text: General. Consultant shall secure and maintain, throughout the duration of this Agreement, insurance (on an occurrence basis unless otherwise agreed in writing) of such types and in at least such amounts as required herein. The City shall be named as  an additional insured for all coverages required herein except workers’ compensation coverage and professional liability coverage. All insurance procured for this Agreement by the Consultant, including additional insured designations, shall be primary and noncontributory. Consultant shall provide certificates of insurance on forms acceptable to the City at the time of this Agreement’s execution. The Certificate shall specify the date when such insurance expires. A renewal certificate shall be furnished to the City before the expiration date of any coverage. The City shall be notified by receipt of written notice from the insurer at least 30 days before material modification or cancellation of any policy listed on the Certificate.
suggestions.suggested_fix: General. Consultant shall secure and maintain, throughout the duration of this Agreement and for a period of two (2) years following its expiration or termination, insurance (on an occurrence basis unless otherwise agreed in writing) of such types and in at least such amounts as required herein. The maintenance of insurance as required herein shall not be construed to limit the liability of either party under this Agreement. The City shall be named as an additional insured for all coverages required herein except workers' compensation coverage and professional liability coverage. All insurance procured for this Agreement by the Consultant, including additional insured designations, shall be primary and noncontributory. Consultant shall provide certificates of insurance on forms acceptable to the City at the time of this Agreement's execution. The Certificate shall specify the date when such insurance expires. A renewal certificate shall be furnished to the City before the expiration date of any coverage. The City shall be notified by receipt of written notice from the insurer at least 30 days before material modification or cancellation of any policy listed on the Certificate.

suggestions.reason: The clause addresses notice by the Consultant but omits the remaining standard claims-handling mechanics—specifically, Consultant's right to control the defense, the City's cooperation obligation, and any settlement consent requirement—leaving both parties without clear procedural guardrails once a claim arises. Additionally, the clause is silent on whether this indemnification obligation is subject to or carved out from any limitation of liability provision elsewhere in the Agreement, creating meaningful uncertainty about the practical scope of the indemnity. Finally, the clause imposes no mitigation obligation on the indemnified party, which is a standard bilateral protection that reduces overall exposure for both parties. These gaps collectively reduce enforceability and operational clarity, and the relationship between this provision and any limitation of liability clause in the Agreement should be expressly addressed.
suggestions.original_text: Section 9. Indemnification. Without in any way limiting indemnification obligations that may be set forth elsewhere in this Agreement, Consultant shall defend, indemnify, and hold harmless the  City, its elected officials, officers, employees, and agents, from all claims, damages, losses, liabilities, costs, and expenses, including attorneys’ fees, arising out of or resulting from the performance of Consultant’s services, provided that any such claim, damage, loss, liability, cost, or expense is caused in whole or in part by a negligent and/or intentional act, error, or omission of the Consultant, its subcontractors, anyone directly or indirectly employed or retained by any of them, or anyone for whose acts any of them may be liable, whether or not arising before or after completion of Consultant’s services. Consultant shall give the City immediate written notice of any claim, suit, or demand that may be subject to this provision.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Section 9. Indemnification. Without in any way limiting indemnification obligations that may be set forth elsewhere in this Agreement, Consultant shall defend, indemnify, and hold harmless the City, its elected officials, officers, employees, and agents, from all claims, damages, losses, liabilities, costs, and expenses, including attorneys' fees, arising out of or resulting from the performance of Consultant's services, provided that any such claim, damage, loss, liability, cost, or expense is caused in whole or in part by a negligent and/or intentional act, error, or omission of the Consultant, its subcontractors, anyone directly or indirectly employed or retained by any of them, or anyone for whose acts any of them may be liable, whether or not arising before or after completion of Consultant's services. This indemnification obligation shall not be limited or reduced by any limitation of liability provision set forth elsewhere in this Agreement. Consultant shall give the City immediate written notice of any claim, suit, or demand that may be subject to this provision. Consultant shall have the right to control the defense and settlement of any such claim, provided that no settlement imposing any obligation or restriction on the City shall be made without the City's prior written consent. Each party shall cooperate reasonably with the other in the defense of any such claim, and the City shall take reasonable steps to mitigate any loss or damage subject to indemnification under this provision.

suggestions.reason: The clause omits governing law entirely and fails to designate any specific forum for resolving disputes, leaving both the City and Consultant without a binding, enforceable mechanism once negotiations fail. The current fallback — permitting the initiating party to "take such steps as it deems necessary" — imposes no mutual forum obligation and effectively grants the claimant unilateral procedural latitude, which creates jurisdictional uncertainty and litigation risk for either party. The continue-performance obligation is also one-sided, binding only the Consultant while imposing no reciprocal obligation on the City to perform its own obligations (including payment) during a dispute. Additionally, neither party is expressly permitted to seek urgent interim or emergency relief, which is a material omission in a professional services context.
suggestions.original_text: Section 11. Disputes. The City and Consultant agree that disputes relative to the Contract Services of this Agreement should first be addressed by negotiations between the parties. If direct negotiations fail to resolve the dispute, the party initiating the claim that is the basis of the dispute shall be free to take such steps as it deems necessary to protect its interest; provided, however, that notwithstanding any such dispute, the Consultant shall proceed with its services under this Agreement as though no dispute exists.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Section 11. Disputes. This Agreement shall be governed by the laws of [State]. The City and Consultant agree that disputes relative to the Contract Services of this Agreement shall first be addressed by good faith negotiations for a period of thirty (30) days following written notice of the dispute by either party. If direct negotiations fail to resolve the dispute within such period, either party may pursue its claims in the courts of [State/County], to which both parties hereby consent to jurisdiction; provided that either party may seek urgent interim relief from a court of competent jurisdiction at any time without first completing the negotiation period. Notwithstanding any such dispute, both parties shall continue to perform their respective obligations under this Agreement.

suggestions.reason: The existing representations clause contains only a single anti-collusion warranty regarding pricing and is silent on four commercially material elements: a standard of performance for the Services, compliance with applicable laws by both parties, a warranty that the Services and deliverables do not infringe third-party intellectual property rights, and a remedy available to the receiving party upon breach of any warranty. This creates significant exposure for both parties: the service recipient has no contractual basis to demand re-performance or a refund if the Services are delivered carelessly or unlawfully, and the service provider has no corresponding protection from claims arising from the recipient's own legal non-compliance. These omissions are particularly material in a Professional Services Agreement where service quality, regulatory obligations, and IP ownership are central commercial concerns.
suggestions.original_text: The price submitted and the costs comprising same are independently arrived at without collusion.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Each party represents and warrants that it shall comply with all applicable laws in the performance of its obligations under this Agreement. Provider further represents and warrants that: (a) the Services shall be performed with reasonable professional skill and care; (b) the Services and any deliverables shall not infringe any third party's intellectual property rights; and (c) the price submitted and the costs comprising the same are independently arrived at without collusion. In the event of a breach of any warranty set forth in this Section, Provider shall, at its option, re-perform the non-conforming Services or refund the fees paid for such non-conforming Services.

suggestions.reason: The authority representation is made exclusively by the Consultant, leaving no equivalent warranty from the Client that it has the requisite power and authority to enter into, and perform its obligations under, the Agreement. This asymmetry creates an enforceability gap: if the Client lacks proper authorization or its signatory acts without authority, the Consultant has no contractual basis to challenge the validity of the arrangement or seek redress grounded in a reciprocal warranty. Market-standard professional services agreements require both parties to represent authority mutually, and the absence of a Client-side warranty is a material structural imbalance in this representations clause.
suggestions.original_text: Consultant has all requisite power and authority to conduct its business and to execute, deliver, and perform the Agreement.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Each party has all requisite power and authority to conduct its business and to execute, deliver, and perform the Agreement, and the individuals who have signed this Agreement on behalf of each party have the legal power, right, and authority to make this Agreement and to bind the respective party.

suggestions.reason: The clause relies on two objectively indefinite performance standards — "recognized professional standards prevalent in their field" and "state of the art procedures and techniques in all relevant subject matters" — neither of which is defined in the clause or, apparently, elsewhere in the Agreement, leaving both parties unable to determine with certainty what level of performance is contractually required. "State of the art" in particular sets an aspirational and potentially ever-shifting benchmark that could expose the Consultant to disproportionate and effectively uncapped warranty liability, while simultaneously giving the client a vague and difficult-to-enforce remedy. The third sentence compounds the ambiguity by using "shall be capable," which imposes an ongoing obligation framed as a state of being rather than a verifiable representation, with no corresponding acknowledgment of the client's obligation to provide information or cooperation necessary for the Consultant to perform. Replacing these indefinite standards with the objectively assessable "standard of care generally observed by qualified professionals providing similar services" resolves the enforceability risk for both parties and aligns the clause with market-standard professional services drafting.
suggestions.original_text: Section 13. Quality Assurance. Consultant warrants that all work and services performed under this Agreement, shall conform to or exceed the recognized professional standards prevalent in their field. Further, the Consultant warrants that all work and service performed under this Agreement shall be performed with the professional expertise, skills, and knowledge of state of the art procedures and techniques in all relevant subject matters. The Consultant accordingly shall be capable of performing the necessary consulting and other services required herein and possess the ready comprehension of the required subject matter and the expertise to provide these services.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Section 13. Quality Assurance. Consultant warrants that all work and services performed under this Agreement shall conform to the standard of care generally observed by qualified professionals providing similar services in the relevant industry. Further, Consultant warrants that all work and services performed under this Agreement shall be performed with professional expertise, skills, and knowledge of professionally accepted procedures and techniques applicable to the relevant subject matter. Consultant accordingly represents that it is capable of performing the necessary consulting and other services required herein and possesses the requisite knowledge of the required subject matter and the expertise to provide these services.

suggestions.reason: The clause as drafted is structurally one-sided: only Consultant is restricted from assigning the Agreement, while the City retains an unchecked ability to assign with no reciprocal limitation. Equally, the City's consent right is unfettered — there is no standard of reasonableness and no response deadline — which could allow consent to be withheld arbitrarily or indefinitely. The provision is also silent on three commercially important scenarios: assignment to affiliates or upon a merger or sale of a business, the obligation of the assigning party to remain liable following a permitted transfer, and notification to the non-assigning party when a transfer occurs, all of which are market-standard elements in a professional services assignment clause.
suggestions.original_text: Section 14. Assignment. Neither this Agreement nor any rights or obligations hereunder shall be assigned or otherwise transferred by Consultant without the prior written consent of the City. This Agreement is binding upon and fully enforceable against the successors and assigns of Consultant, whether consented to or not.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Section 14. Assignment. Neither this Agreement nor any rights or obligations hereunder shall be assigned or otherwise transferred by either party without the prior written consent of the other party, such consent not to be unreasonably withheld, conditioned, or delayed; provided that either party may, upon written notice to the other party, assign this Agreement to an affiliate or to a successor in connection with a merger, acquisition, or sale of all or substantially all of its assets or business. No permitted assignment shall relieve the assigning party of its obligations under this Agreement unless expressly released in writing by the other party. This Agreement is binding upon and fully enforceable against the permitted successors and assigns of both parties.

suggestions.reason: The notices clause sets out Columbia Capital Management, LLC's contact details but contains no mechanism by which either party may update its notice information during the term of the Agreement. Without such a mechanism, a party that relocates, changes its designated contact, or updates its address has no contractual means to redirect notices, creating a risk that notices sent to stale details are deemed validly delivered while the intended recipient remains unaware. This gap affects both parties equally and could impair the exercise of time-sensitive rights elsewhere in the Agreement, such as breach notices or termination triggers, that depend on valid delivery.
suggestions.original_text: Columbia Capital Management, LLC Attn: Compliance Officer 6700 Antioch Rd., Suite 250 Merriam, KS 66204
suggestions.suggested_fix:
Columbia Capital Management, LLC Attn: Compliance Officer 6700 Antioch Rd., Suite 250 Merriam, KS 66204

Either party may change its notice details by providing written notice of the updated information to the other party, effective ten (10) days following receipt of such notice.

suggestions.reason: The clause omits three market-standard elements that are critical to establishing a defensible independent contractor relationship: it does not state that Consultant retains control over the manner and means of performing the Services, it places tax and cost obligations solely on Consultant without addressing the City's corresponding responsibility for its own personnel, and it fails to state that neither party has authority to bind the other. The absence of these elements creates legal and operational exposure for both parties — a court or tax authority assessing the true nature of the relationship would find the clause incomplete, and the lack of mutual no-authority language leaves each party exposed to unauthorized commitments purportedly made on its behalf.
suggestions.original_text: Section 16. Independent Contractor. In no event, while performing under this Agreement, shall Consultant be deemed to be acting as an employee of the City; rather, Consultant shall be deemed to be an independent contractor. Consultant shall be responsible for and pay all taxes and withholdings required by law upon the compensation paid under this Agreement, and shall defend, indemnify, and hold harmless the City from liability in connection therewith. Nothing expressed herein or implied herein shall be construed as creating between Consultant and the City the relationships of employer and employee, principal and agent, a partnership, or a joint venture.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Section 16. Independent Contractor. In no event, while performing under this Agreement, shall Consultant be deemed to be acting as an employee of the City; rather, Consultant shall be deemed to be an independent contractor who retains sole control over the manner and means of performing the Services. Each party shall be responsible for the compensation, taxes, withholdings, and benefits of its own respective personnel. Consultant shall defend, indemnify, and hold harmless the City from liability arising from Consultant's failure to discharge such obligations with respect to Consultant's personnel. Neither party shall have authority to bind or obligate the other party. Nothing expressed herein or implied herein shall be construed as creating between Consultant and the City the relationships of employer and employee, principal and agent, a partnership, or a joint venture.

suggestions.clause: Compliance with Kansas Cash Basis Law
suggestions.reason: The clause addresses only the Kansas Cash Basis Law and budget-appropriation mechanics, leaving material compliance gaps that create legal and operational risk for both parties: there is no general obligation to comply with applicable law, no anti-bribery or corruption commitment, no requirement to notify the other party of a legal breach affecting performance, no allocation of the cost and effort of adapting to a change in law, and no supply-chain labor standards covering forced labor or human trafficking. These omissions are commercially significant in a Professional Services Agreement involving a government entity, where regulatory exposure, public accountability, and service-chain integrity are heightened concerns. The absence of a notification obligation in particular means a party could be in breach of law for an extended period without the other party having any contractual basis to respond or seek relief.
suggestions.original_text: Section 17. Compliance with Kansas Cash Basis Law. This Agreement must comply with the applicable provisions of the Kansas Cash-Basis Law, K.S.A. 10-1101 et seq., as amended. The City is obligated only to pay periodic payments or monthly installments under this Agreement as may lawfully be made from funds budgeted and appropriated for the purposes set forth in this Agreement during the City’s current budget year. Notwithstanding any other provision of this Agreement, in the event that the City does not budget and appropriate funds for any renewal term, for any reason in its sole discretion, the parties agree that they shall be relieved of all obligations under this Agreement without penalty. To the extent that the City does budget and appropriate funds for the purposes set forth in this Agreement, the obligations of the parties shall remain as provided herein.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Section 17. Compliance with Laws. Each party shall comply with all applicable laws and regulations, including those prohibiting bribery, corruption, forced labor, child labor, and human trafficking in its supply chain. Each party shall promptly notify the other in writing if it becomes aware of any breach of applicable law that materially affects performance of this Agreement, and the cost of complying with any change in applicable law shall be borne by the party upon whom such obligation is imposed by law. This Agreement must comply with the applicable provisions of the Kansas Cash-Basis Law, K.S.A. 10-1101 et seq., as amended. The City is obligated only to pay periodic payments or monthly installments under this Agreement as may lawfully be made from funds budgeted and appropriated for the purposes set forth in this Agreement during the City's current budget year. Notwithstanding any other provision of this Agreement, in the event that the City does not budget and appropriate funds for any renewal term, for any reason in its sole discretion, the parties agree that they shall be relieved of all obligations under this Agreement without penalty. To the extent that the City does budget and appropriate funds for the purposes set forth in this Agreement, the obligations of the parties shall remain as provided herein.

suggestions.reason: The clause as drafted addresses only the choice of governing law and is entirely silent on five commercially material elements: the forum in which disputes will be decided, any pre-dispute escalation or negotiation obligation, mutual submission to that forum, the right to seek urgent injunctive relief, and each party's obligation to continue performing during a dispute. Without these provisions, either party may commence formal proceedings in any court without prior notice or escalation, seek to litigate in a convenient but non-agreed jurisdiction, and use a pending dispute as a pretext to suspend performance, all of which expose both parties to unnecessary litigation cost and commercial disruption. The absence of a forum-selection clause also creates a material enforceability gap because the governing-law choice does not, by itself, determine where proceedings must be brought.
suggestions.original_text: Section 19. Governing Law. This Agreement, the rights and obligations of the parties, and any claim or dispute arising hereunder shall be construed in accordance with the laws of the State of Kansas.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Section 19. Governing Law and Dispute Resolution. This Agreement, the rights and obligations of the parties, and any claim or dispute arising hereunder shall be construed in accordance with the laws of the State of Kansas. Prior to initiating formal proceedings, the parties shall attempt to resolve any dispute through good-faith negotiation for a period of thirty (30) days following written notice of the dispute from one party to the other. Any dispute not resolved through such negotiation shall be submitted exclusively to the state or federal courts located in Topeka, Kansas, to whose jurisdiction both parties irrevocably and unconditionally submit. Notwithstanding the foregoing, either party may seek urgent injunctive or other equitable relief from a court of competent jurisdiction without first satisfying the negotiation requirement. Each party shall continue to perform its obligations under this Agreement pending final resolution of any dispute.

suggestions.reason: The phrase "automatically be considered reformed and amended so as to conform to all applicable legal requirements" is operationally ambiguous in two respects: it neither identifies which party or tribunal performs the reformation nor establishes any standard by which the reformed provision is to be measured, leaving the clause's operative effect uncertain. As drafted, two reasonable lawyers could disagree whether "automatically" means the provision self-corrects by contract, requires judicial rewriting, or obliges the parties to negotiate a replacement, which would force recourse to extrinsic evidence in any dispute. The absence of an intent-preservation standard also means that a court could substitute language materially different from what the parties originally agreed, altering the commercial bargain without reference to their original purpose. No survival or cross-reference alignment issues are raised by this provision.
suggestions.original_text: Section 22. Invalidity. If any provision in this Agreement shall be adjudicated invalid under applicable laws, such invalid provision shall automatically be considered reformed and amended so as to conform to all applicable legal requirements, or, if such invalidity cannot be cured by reformation or amendment, the same shall be considered stricken and deleted, but in neither such event or events shall the validity or enforceability of the remaining valid portions hereof be affected thereby.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Section 22. Invalidity. If any provision in this Agreement shall be adjudicated invalid under applicable laws, the parties shall cooperate in good faith to replace such invalid provision with a valid provision that most closely reflects the original intent and commercial effect of the invalid provision to the extent permitted by applicable law, or, if such invalidity cannot be cured by such replacement, the same shall be considered stricken and deleted, but in neither such event or events shall the validity or enforceability of the remaining valid portions hereof be affected thereby.

suggestions.reason: The clause currently addresses non-waiver through inaction and requires writing for any effective waiver, but omits the standard protection that a waiver of one specific breach or right does not operate as a waiver of any other or subsequent breach or right. Without this language, a party that grants a written waiver for a particular breach could face an argument that it has implicitly waived its entitlement to enforce similar or related obligations arising on other occasions. This gap creates enforceability uncertainty for both parties equally, as either party could be exposed to such an argument in a dispute context. The addition of a single non-waiver-of-other-rights sentence resolves this risk without altering the clause's existing structure or balance.
suggestions.original_text: Section 23. Waiver. The failure of either party to insist upon the strict performance of any of the terms or conditions of this Agreement or to exercise any option, right, or remedy herein contained, shall not be construed as a waiver or relinquishment for the future of such term, provision, option, right, or remedy, but the same shall continue and remain in full force and effect. No waiver by either party of any term or provision hereof shall be deemed to have been made unless expressed in writing and signed by the waiving party.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Section 23. Waiver. The failure of either party to insist upon the strict performance of any of the terms or conditions of this Agreement or to exercise any option, right, or remedy herein contained, shall not be construed as a waiver or relinquishment for the future of such term, provision, option, right, or remedy, but the same shall continue and remain in full force and effect. No waiver by either party of any particular breach or right shall constitute a waiver of any other or subsequent breach or right. No waiver by either party of any term or provision hereof shall be deemed to have been made unless expressed in writing and signed by the waiving party.

suggestions.reason: The clause as drafted contains three material gaps that create enforceability and operational risk for both parties equally. First, it does not specify that signatories must be authorized representatives of each party, leaving open the possibility that any employee's signature could be argued to effect a valid amendment. Second, it refers only to "This Agreement" without expressly covering schedules and order forms, which are typically the documents most frequently modified in a professional services relationship, creating ambiguity about whether changes to those instruments require the same written formality. Third, the absence of a no-oral-modification and no-waiver-by-conduct provision means that either party could argue that consistent course of dealing or informal exchanges altered the Agreement's terms, undermining the written-amendment requirement itself.
suggestions.original_text: Section 26. Amendments. This Agreement may not be amended unless such amendment is in writing and signed by both parties.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Section 26. Amendments. This Agreement, including any schedules and order forms, may not be amended except by a written instrument signed by an authorized representative of each party, and no oral agreement or course of conduct shall constitute an amendment or waiver of any provision hereof.

suggestions.reason: The survival clause expressly names only the Consultant's post-termination obligations—Insurance and Indemnification—without reference to any surviving obligations of the Client, such as payment for Services rendered prior to termination or other duties that would logically endure beyond the Agreement's end. This asymmetry means the clause, as drafted, operates unilaterally against one party without commercial justification. Additionally, the catch-all phrase "any other terms and conditions that by their nature should survive termination" is imprecise enough that two reasonable lawyers could disagree as to which provisions it captures, undermining the clause's enforceability and creating post-termination disputes. Replacing "should survive" with "are intended to survive" and extending the catch-all to both parties' obligations corrects the ambiguity and bilateral imbalance without altering the substance of the specifically named provisions.
suggestions.original_text: Section 27. Survivorship. Notwithstanding the termination of this Agreement, Consultant’s obligations with respect to Insurance (Section 8) and Indemnification (Section 9), and any other terms and conditions that by their nature should survive termination, shall survive the termination of this Agreement.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Section 27. Survivorship. Notwithstanding the termination of this Agreement, Consultant's obligations with respect to Insurance (Section 8) and Indemnification (Section 9), and any other obligations of either party that by their nature are intended to survive termination, shall survive the termination of this Agreement.

suggestions.reason: The clause imposes a broad legal compliance obligation exclusively on the Consultant, leaving the City without any corresponding duty to perform its own obligations in accordance with applicable law, which creates an asymmetry without commercial justification. The phrase "responsibilities of investment management" is not defined in the clause or cross-referenced to any schedule or exhibit, leaving the scope of the Consultant's core mandate open to dispute. Additionally, the reference to "all other provisions of law applicable to this undertaking" is insufficiently precise—two reasonable readers could disagree on which legal regime or statutory framework governs—creating an enforceability risk that could be exploited in a dispute over the Consultant's performance standard.
suggestions.original_text: Appointment of Consultant. The City hereby appoints Consultant to act as the investment adviser and to assume the responsibilities of investment management of the pooled cash of the City including all idle funds, cash, deposits, investments, capital accounts and bond proceeds (the “Accounts”). Consultant does hereby accept said appointment as an investment adviser under the Accounts. By accepting such appointment, Consultant agrees that at all times it shall act in accordance with the terms and conditions of this Agreement and all other provisions of law applicable to this undertaking.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Appointment of Consultant. The City hereby appoints Consultant to act as the investment adviser and to assume the responsibilities of investment management, as set forth in this Agreement, of the pooled cash of the City including all idle funds, cash, deposits, investments, capital accounts and bond proceeds (the "Accounts"). Consultant does hereby accept said appointment as an investment adviser under the Accounts. Each party agrees that at all times it shall act in accordance with the terms and conditions of this Agreement and all applicable laws and regulations in the performance of its respective obligations hereunder.

suggestions.reason: The clause imposes a broad, open-ended fiduciary standard on the Consultant, and the additive language expressly layering all applicable federal and state fiduciary duties on top of the contractual obligation creates potentially unlimited liability exposure with no cross-reference to any limitation of liability provision elsewhere in the Agreement. The obligation is entirely unilateral: the Client bears no corresponding duty to provide accurate, complete information or reasonable cooperation, which are preconditions in practice to the Consultant's ability to discharge fiduciary obligations with respect to managed assets. Additionally, the phrase "enterprise of like character and with like aims" introduces interpretive uncertainty about the specific benchmark against which the Consultant's conduct will be assessed, which could be read differently by reasonable counsel depending on the industry or asset class involved. If the Agreement contains a limitation of liability provision, the interaction between that provision and this open-ended fiduciary standard should be expressly addressed.
suggestions.original_text: Fiduciary. In addition to, but not in lieu of any and all applicable fiduciary standards imposed under federal or state law, Consultant shall act as a fiduciary with respect to the assets it manages pursuant to this Agreement. As a fiduciary, Consultant shall perform its duties under this Agreement with the care, skill, prudence, and diligence under the circumstances then prevailing that a prudent person acting in a like capacity and familiar with such matters would use in an enterprise of like character and with like aims.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Fiduciary. In addition to, but not in lieu of any and all applicable fiduciary standards imposed under federal or state law, Consultant shall act as a fiduciary with respect to the assets it manages pursuant to this Agreement, subject to any express limitations on liability set forth in this Agreement. As a fiduciary, Consultant shall perform its duties under this Agreement with the care, skill, prudence, and diligence under the circumstances then prevailing that a prudent person acting in a like capacity and familiar with such matters would use in an enterprise of like character and with like aims. Client shall provide Consultant with accurate and complete information and reasonable cooperation as necessary to enable Consultant to discharge its fiduciary obligations under this Agreement.

suggestions.reason: The word "Timely" sets no objectively measurable performance standard, leaving both parties unable to determine when the City's obligation is triggered, satisfied, or breached. Without a defined frequency or deadline, the Consultant cannot rely on a predictable data flow to implement the investment plan, and the City cannot know when it is in default of this duty. This ambiguity exposes both parties to dispute over whether the obligation has been performed and undermines the operational foundation on which the Consultant's advisory services depend.
suggestions.original_text: Timely provide Consultant with balances, account statements and interest earned on the City’s funds and accounts.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Provide Consultant, within five (5) Business Days following the close of each calendar month, with balances, account statements and interest earned on the City's funds and accounts.

suggestions.reason: The clause imposes an open-ended, unqualified obligation on the City to supply financial data at the Consultant's sole discretion, with no timeframe within which the City must respond and no reciprocal obligation on the Consultant regarding how that data may be used. This asymmetry means the Consultant may request sensitive account information at any time and for any purpose, while the City bears the entire burden of performance without any corresponding duty imposed on the Consultant. From a bilateral fairness standpoint, the absence of a response period leaves the City's obligation commercially unworkable, and the absence of a use-limitation obligation on the Consultant creates an unreciprocated information right with no accountability.
suggestions.original_text: Upon request, provide Consultant with historical account balances and monthly account cash flows to permit Consultant to properly determine required liquidity.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Upon written request, provide Consultant with historical account balances and monthly account cash flows within a reasonable time following such request to permit Consultant to properly determine required liquidity; Consultant shall use such information solely for that purpose and shall not disclose it to any third party without the City's prior written consent.

suggestions.reason: The phrase "investment plan" is not defined in this clause or, apparently, elsewhere in the Agreement, leaving both parties without a clear, enforceable reference point for which fund movements the City is obligated to execute. This ambiguity exposes the City to disputed or unauthorized transfer requests and leaves the Consultant without certainty as to the scope of its authority to direct account movements. Without anchoring this obligation to a written, mutually agreed investment plan, neither party has a reliable standard against which compliance or refusal can be measured, creating meaningful operational and legal risk for both sides.
suggestions.original_text: Upon request and with reasonable notice, respond to Consultant’s requests to move money via Federal Reserve wire or other means between the City’s various accounts as necessary to effect the investment plan.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Upon request and with reasonable notice, respond to Consultant's requests to move money via Federal Reserve wire or other means between the City's various accounts as necessary to effect the written investment plan agreed upon in writing by the City and the Consultant (the "Investment Plan").

suggestions.reason: The clause places the full financial burden of "all expenses relating to the purchase and sale of such securities" on the City without limiting that exposure to amounts expressly authorized by Consultant, creating open-ended liability that could encompass unanticipated or unauthorized costs. Additionally, the phrase "copies of confirmations provided to the Custodian by Consultant" is undefined — it does not specify the required form, content, or timing of those confirmations — making the City's instruction obligation difficult to enforce and creating execution ambiguity if confirmations are delayed, incomplete, or disputed. No timeline is imposed on when the City must act following receipt of a confirmation, nor is any corresponding obligation placed on Consultant to deliver confirmations within a defined period, leaving both parties without a workable operational framework. These deficiencies create asymmetric exposure and enforceability risk for both sides.
suggestions.original_text: Custodian. Pursuant to K.S.A. 12-1675(e)(1) the City shall instruct the Custodian to deliver securities sold and pay for securities purchased, including all expenses relating to the purchase and sale of such securities, such as brokerage commissions and transfer taxes, in accordance with copies of confirmations provided to the Custodian by Consultant.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Custodian. Pursuant to K.S.A. 12-1675(e)(1), the City shall instruct the Custodian, within two (2) Business Days following receipt of a written confirmation from Consultant, to deliver securities sold and pay for securities purchased, including all expenses expressly authorized in such written confirmation, such as brokerage commissions and transfer taxes. Consultant shall provide written confirmations to the Custodian and the City within one (1) Business Day following each transaction.

suggestions.reason: The clause describes Consultant's existing policy for managing potential conflicts through equitable allocation and bond purchase restrictions, but it does not impose any affirmative obligation on Consultant to disclose actual or potential conflicts to the City when they arise. Without a mandatory disclosure obligation, the City has no mechanism to identify conflicts that fall outside the specific bond-purchase policy described, leaving it exposed to undisclosed conflicts that could materially affect the management of the Accounts. From a bilateral fairness standpoint, an ongoing disclosure requirement is a market-standard element of any fiduciary or advisory relationship and is necessary to give both parties a workable means of addressing conflicts as they emerge.
suggestions.original_text: Potential Conflicts of Consultant. It is understood that Consultant will be acting in a similar capacity for other institutional clients, including other municipal governments in Kansas and that investments and reinvestments for the Accounts of the City may differ from those made or recommended with respect to the accounts and clients even though the investment objectives may be the same or similar; however, Consultant shall allocate investment opportunities among clients on a fair and equitable basis. In addition, Consultant serves as financial advisor to municipal governments within and beyond Kansas that issue bonds (an “Issuer Client”), including, in the case of Kansas issuers, bonds eligible for investment by the City. To prevent any appearances of favoring an issuer client over an investment client, or of favoring an investment client over an issuer client, it is the policy of Consultant to not purchase bonds of an Issuer Client issuing bonds in the primary market on behalf an investing client or to purchase callable bonds of an Issuer Client at any time on behalf of an investing client. This policy serves to protect both clients from potential conflicts but may limit investment opportunities for the City from time to time.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Potential Conflicts of Consultant. It is understood that Consultant will be acting in a similar capacity for other institutional clients, including other municipal governments in Kansas and that investments and reinvestments for the Accounts of the City may differ from those made or recommended with respect to the accounts and clients even though the investment objectives may be the same or similar; however, Consultant shall allocate investment opportunities among clients on a fair and equitable basis. Consultant shall promptly disclose to the City any actual or potential conflict of interest of which it becomes aware that may affect its performance of services under this Agreement. In addition, Consultant serves as financial advisor to municipal governments within and beyond Kansas that issue bonds (an "Issuer Client"), including, in the case of Kansas issuers, bonds eligible for investment by the City. To prevent any appearances of favoring an issuer client over an investment client, or of favoring an investment client over an issuer client, it is the policy of Consultant to not purchase bonds of an Issuer Client issuing bonds in the primary market on behalf of an investing client or to purchase callable bonds of an Issuer Client at any time on behalf of an investing client. This policy serves to protect both clients from potential conflicts but may limit investment opportunities for the City from time to time.

suggestions.reason: The amendment provision allows the City to modify Schedule X "at any time" with mere unqualified "notice" to Consultant, specifying neither the form nor the advance period of that notice, which leaves Consultant with no operational lead time to adjust to changes in authorized personnel or their authorities. This ambiguity means two reasonable parties could dispute whether a same-day email satisfies the notice requirement, undermining the enforceability of the amendment mechanism. Additionally, the reference to "Schedule X" is an unfilled placeholder that must be replaced with the actual schedule identifier prior to execution. The permission for Consultant to use Account information in "aggregate performance data" is also commercially ambiguous, as "aggregate performance data" is undefined and without a de-identification qualifier could invite dispute over the scope of that data use right.
suggestions.original_text: Directions to Consultant. The names, titles and authorities of the individuals authorized to act on behalf of the City with respect to the Accounts and this Agreement are set forth in Schedule X to this Agreement, which is attached hereto and incorporated herein, and which may be amended in writing at any time by the City with notice provided to Consultant. Consultant may include information regarding the Accounts in aggregate performance data of Consultant that does not identify the City.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Directions to Consultant. The names, titles and authorities of the individuals authorized to act on behalf of the City with respect to the Accounts and this Agreement are set forth in Schedule X to this Agreement, which is attached hereto and incorporated herein, and which may be amended in writing by the City upon at least ten (10) days' prior written notice to Consultant. Consultant may include de-identified information regarding the Accounts in aggregate performance data of Consultant that does not identify the City.

suggestions.reason: The clause establishes the fee rate and calculation methodology but omits several commercially essential payment mechanics: no invoice issuance date is specified, no payment due date is stated, the fee rate contains no change-notice requirement, there is no mechanism for disputing an invoice, no late-payment consequence is provided, and the "sole compensation" language does not expressly address whether pre-approved out-of-pocket expenses are reimbursable. Taken together, these omissions create material uncertainty for both parties regarding payment obligations, enforcement rights, and the full scope of compensation, increasing the risk of fee disputes and collection difficulties. The absence of an expense treatment provision is particularly important given that the "sole compensation" sentence could be read to preclude expense reimbursement entirely, which may not reflect the parties' commercial intent.
suggestions.original_text: Management Fees. Consultant will be compensated for its services under this Agreement in an amount equal to 0.20% of the market value of the Accounts, billed quarterly in arrears based upon the average of the month-end Account balances for such quarter, with a minimum fee for each quarter of $3,000. Market value, including accrued income, will be determinative for the purpose of calculating fees. Such amount shall be the sole compensation owing by reason of investment advisory services under this Agreement. The fee for services for any period less than a full quarterly period will be pro-rated on a daily basis on the annualized fee for the period and on the market value of the portfolio as described on the final date of such period.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Management Fees. Consultant will be compensated for its services under this Agreement in an amount equal to 0.20% of the market value of the Accounts, billed quarterly in arrears based upon the average of the month-end Account balances for such quarter, with a minimum fee for each quarter of $3,000. Invoices shall be issued within fifteen (15) days following the end of each quarter and shall be due and payable within thirty (30) days of receipt. Any disputed portion of an invoice shall be held in abeyance pending written resolution by the parties, while undisputed amounts remain due on the original payment date. Overdue undisputed amounts shall bear interest at 1.5% per month or the maximum rate permitted by applicable law, whichever is lower. The fee rate may be adjusted upon not less than thirty (30) days' prior written notice to Client. Market value, including accrued income, will be determinative for the purpose of calculating fees. Such amount shall be the sole compensation owing by reason of investment advisory services under this Agreement, excluding pre-approved out-of-pocket expenses, which shall be reimbursed by Client upon presentation of reasonable supporting documentation. The fee for services for any period less than a full quarterly period will be pro-rated on a daily basis on the annualized fee for the period and on the market value of the portfolio as described on the final date of such period.

suggestions.reason: The clause imposes an unconditional obligation on the City to direct the Custodian in the voting of all proxies while granting the Consultant a blanket exemption from any responsibility, without establishing any corresponding obligation on the Consultant to support the City's exercise of that authority. This one-sidedness creates a gap: the City bears the entire operational burden of directing proxy votes with no contractual basis to call upon the Consultant for guidance or recommendations. Additionally, the phrase "in voting of all proxies" is grammatically incomplete, creating ambiguity as to the scope and mechanics of the City's direction obligation that a court would need extrinsic evidence to resolve.
suggestions.original_text: Proxy Voting. The City shall direct the Custodian in voting of all proxies and Consultant shall have no responsibility in respect of the voting of proxies.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Proxy Voting. The City shall direct the Custodian in the voting of all proxies, and Consultant shall have no responsibility with respect to the voting of proxies, provided that Consultant shall provide proxy voting recommendations upon the City's written request.

suggestions.reason: The clause as drafted limits Consultant's representations solely to investment adviser registration status and Form ADV delivery, leaving three material gaps: there is no warranty of compliance with applicable laws beyond registration, no representation that the Services are free from third-party intellectual property infringement, and no stated warranty period or remedy upon breach. Without these elements, the City has no defined contractual basis to seek re-performance or a refund if the Services are legally non-compliant or infringe third-party rights, and Consultant's exposure is effectively undefined in scope and duration. These omissions also create an asymmetry that undermines the bilateral enforceability of the certification framework.
suggestions.original_text: Consultant (i) is registered as an “investment adviser” under the Investment  Consultants Act of 1940 as amended (the “Consultants Act”); (ii) will promptly advise the City if at any time during the term of this Agreement Consultant ceases being so registered; and (iii) has delivered to the City a copy of Part II of its Form ADV or comparable Brochure pursuant to the Consultants Act;
suggestions.suggested_fix: Consultant (i) is registered as an "investment adviser" under the Investment Consultants Act of 1940 as amended (the "Consultants Act"); (ii) will promptly advise the City if at any time during the term of this Agreement Consultant ceases being so registered; (iii) has delivered to the City a copy of Part II of its Form ADV or comparable Brochure pursuant to the Consultants Act; (iv) is in compliance with all applicable laws in performing the Services; and (v) the Services will not infringe any third-party intellectual property rights. The foregoing representations and warranties apply throughout the term of this Agreement, and upon breach, Consultant shall re-perform the affected Services or, if re-performance is not practicable, refund the fees paid therefor.

suggestions.reason: The authority representation is unilateral: only the Consultant warrants that it is duly authorized to execute, deliver, and perform the Agreement, while no equivalent representation is made by the Company. In a bilateral Professional Services Agreement, the absence of a matching authority representation from the Company creates an enforcement asymmetry — if the Company lacked proper authorization, the Consultant would have no contractual basis to challenge the validity of the Agreement on that ground. Mutual authority representations are a market-standard baseline in commercial agreements, and the gap leaves the enforceability of the arrangement one-sided.
suggestions.original_text: Consultant is duly authorized and fully empowered to execute, deliver and perform this Agreement.
suggestions.suggested_fix: Each party represents that it is duly authorized and fully empowered to execute, deliver and perform this Agreement.
